_comment: Loan-success-score component weights, per position. Unlike data/score_weights.json (permanent transfers), there's no value_for_money or resale_profit component: most loans carry no real fee (the packaged fee is 0 even when a real loan fee was agreed - see fetch_transfer_types.py), and a loan doesn't end in a sale of its own. playing_time is weighted heavily across every position - whether the loan actually delivered game time is usually the central question a loan gets judged on, independent of how well the player performed when they did play. value_growth and rating are both deliberately FLAT across every position (0.12/0.10), same reasoning as data/score_weights.json: value_growth is a single global percentile rank with no position grouping, so there's no football-role reason for its weight to vary by position; rating is the same metric (FotMob's overall per-match quality score) regardless of role, unlike attacking/defensive/possession which are literally different stats by position, and was previously underweighted (2-9%) relative to how holistic a signal it is. rating's move up to flat 0.10 is funded from perf_level/perf_delta/playing_time (scaled down proportionally) rather than from value_growth (already flat) or attacking/defensive/possession (kept as tuned). Each FotMob component is only known for the loans FotMob has tenure stats for (scripts/fetch_fotmob_stats.py, same fetch as permanent transfers) - its weight is dropped and the rest renormalized for a loan missing it, same pattern as data/score_weights.json. Shared by scripts/build_dataset.py (computes the label) and app/main.py (labels the 'why this score' explanation). Each position row must sum to 1.0.
_sub_positions_comment: Sub-position weight overrides, same idea and same rows as data/score_weights.json's _sub_positions (see that file's comment for the full rationale) - a player's actual career-wide fielded sub-position selects one of these rows instead of the broad position row above when one exists; percentile ranking still groups by the broad position. value_growth and rating are flat 0.12/0.10 here too, same as the broad rows above and for the same reason - neither has a football-role basis to vary at this level either. Full-back's defensive is raised to 0.22 (funded from perf_level/perf_delta/attacking, same as the permanent-transfer table) - capped below Centre-Back's 0.24 rather than matching the permanent table's 0.26 exactly, since a full-back shouldn't out-weight a centre-back on defending.
